{{nihongo|'''Hikawa Nyotai Shrine'''|氷川女体神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Hikawa Nyotai Shrine''' (ひかわにょたいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Midori-ku, Saitama|ceb|Midori-ku (subdistrito sa Hapon, Saitama-ken)|de|Midori-ku (Saitama)|eo|Midori-ku (Sajtama)|fa|میدوری-کو، سایتاما|fr|Midori-ku (Saitama)|id|Midori-ku, Saitama|it|Midori-ku (Saitama)|ja|緑区 (さいたま市)|ko|미도리구 (사이타마시)|th|เขตมิโดริ (ไซตามะ)|tr|Midori, Saitama|uk|Мідорі (район, Сайтама)|ur|میدوری وارڈ، سائیتاما|vi|Midori, Saitama|zh|綠區 (埼玉市)|qid=Q1130733|lt=Midori Ward}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|Q128186|qid=Q128186}}. Its registered {{ill|religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qid=Q7311343}} name uses old characters: '''氷川女體神社'''<ref>{{Cite web |ja |url=https://www.houjin-bangou.nta.go.jp/henkorireki-johoto.html?selHouzinNo=8030005000159 |title=Information on Hikawa Nyotai Shrine |website=National Tax Agency Corporate Number Publication Site |access-date=2024-01-02}}</ref>. It styles itself as a {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. It is a member of the National Ichinomiya Association. Its former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank}} was {{ill|Q712534|lt=Gōsha}}.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the era of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} by inviting the deity from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|Q696362|qid=Q696362}}.

'Dai Nihon Chimei Jisho' identifies it as a candidate shrine for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} “{{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}{{ill|Adachi district|de|Adachi-gun (Musashi)|ja|足立郡|ko|아다치군 (무사시국)|qid=Q11637033}} Takehime Shrine” listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}},' but the stronger theory is that Takehime Shrine is {{ill|Takehime Shrine (Q65734340)|Q65734340|qid=Q65734340}} in Shinotsu, {{ill|Okegawa, Saitama|Q570333|qid=Q570333}}.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19 ({{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} donated 50 koku of shrine land{{Sfn|井上|1998|p=89}}.

Early-modern documents and the plaque on the worship hall describe it as “{{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}.” This interprets Ōmiya Hikawa Shrine, this shrine, and {{ill|Nakayama Shrine|Q11364245|qid=Q11364245|lt=Nakayama Shrine}} (Hioji-sha) as a unified complex; since Ōmiya Hikawa Shrine is Musashi Ichinomiya, this shrine is considered included in that status (see below). Also, this is said to be the birthplace of Ichinomiya pilgrimage, as {{ill|Tachibana Mitsuyoshi|Q11544184|qid=Q11544184}} began his circuit from here in the Edo period. For these reasons, it is now, together with Hikawa Shrine, a member of the National Ichinomiya Association.

In the '{{ill|Edo meisho zue|Q2704637|qid=Q2704637}},' it is listed under the shrine name “Moto-Hikawa Shrine.”

=== The three Hikawa shrines around Minuma ===
{| class="wikitable" style="float:right"
! Shrine !! Alias !! Principal deity !! Relationship
|-
|'''Hikawa Shrine'''
| Male-body shrine ||{{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}|| Husband
|-
|'''Hikawa Nyotai Shrine'''
| Female-body shrine ||{{ill|Kushinadahime|lt=Kushinadahime|Q505469|qid=Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushinadahime-no-Mikoto}}|| Wife
|-
| '''Nakayama Shrine'''<br />{{Small|(Naka-Hikawa Shrine)}}
| Hioji-sha<br />{{Small|(Hioji-sha)}} ||{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}|| Child (descendant)

This shrine, Hikawa Shrine, and Nakayama Shrine—located near former {{ill|Minuma|Q6869769|qid=Q6869769}}—lie on a straight line{{Sfn|青木|1984|p=11}}. The {{ill|Sun|Q525|qid=Q525}} sets at summer solstice in the west-northwest at Hikawa Shrine, and rises at winter solstice from the east-southeast at Hikawa Nyotai Shrine, an intentional arrangement to accurately track the {{ill|Calendar|Q12132|qid=Q12132}} important for {{ill|Rice Cultivation|Q734080|qid=Q734080}}. The relationship among the three shrines is as shown in the table at right.

From this, one theory holds that the three formed a unified Hikawa shrine complex, with Minuma as a sacred pond “Onuma,” creating a vast sacred domain<ref>{{Cite book |ja |author=Ōmiya City |author-link=Ōmiya City |title=Past and Present of Ōmiya |publisher=Ōmiya City |date=1980-11 |id={{JP番号|81007009}} |page=28}}</ref>.
{{Clear|right}}

=== Precincts ===
* Main sanctuary
** In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 7 ({{ill|1667|Q7588|qid=Q7588}}), fourth shogun {{ill|Tokugawa Ietsuna|Q323422|qid=Q323422}} ordered {{ill|Abe Tadaaki|Q4666449|qid=Q4666449}}, lord of {{ill|Oshi Castle|Q1074393|qid=Q1074393}}, to rebuild it. The ridge-tag from this reconstruction reads “Musashi Ichinomiya Hikawa Nyotai Daimyōjin,” bearing the Musashi Ichinomiya title.
* Iwafune Festival ritual site ruins
** At the end of the Miyuki path in front of the precincts is the “Iwafune Festival Ritual Site Ruins.” Originally, the most important ritual of Hikawa Nyotai Shrine was the Ofune Festival held at {{ill|Minuma|Q6869769|qid=Q6869769}}. However, in {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 13 (1728), Minuma was reclaimed and the Ofune Festival could no longer be held there. Therefore, in the following year, a ritual site with a round island in a pond was established at what had been part of Minuma, and an “Iwafune Festival” was held in place of the Ofune Festival. The Iwafune Festival ceased by early Meiji, but the ruins remain in good preservation{{Sfn|井上|1998|p=14}}.

Multiple shrines stand behind the main sanctuary.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Art Object (nationally recognized) ===
* Mitsurin-mon Hyōgo-kusari tachi, 1 sword - recognized April 27, 1948 (Shōwa 23)

=== Saitama Prefecture-designated tangible cultural properties ===
* Mitsurin-mon Hyōgo-kusari tachi, 1 sword (craft) - designated March 28, 1972 (same item as the nationally recognized Important Art Object){{Sfn|浦和市教育委員会|2000|p=5}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |ja |url=https://www.city.saitama.lg.jp/004/005/006/003/p001267_d/fil/bunkazaiitiran.pdf |title=List of designated/registered cultural properties in Saitama City |publisher=Saitama City |date=2024-08-01 |access-date=2024-10-04}}</ref>
